svg.title: Slab-ocean step: algorithm flow
svg.desc: One slab-ocean step. The state carried in is the mixed-layer SST T_o, the mixed-layer depth H, the ice thickness h_i, the surface heat flux Q_a passed down by the ice step and averaged over the coupling window, the deep-ocean heat flux Q_deep and the interpolated monthly SST climatology T_clim; the heat capacity is C_o = rho_o c_p,o H and the step is dt_mix = N T_sol / N_tspd. Q_deep comes from the three-dimensional ocean, which runs first with its top layer reset to T_o, and is zero in a slab build. Ice-free points update the SST explicitly, T_o* = T_o^n + dt_mix (Q_a + Q_deep) / (rho_o c_p,o H), while ice-covered points keep T_o* = T_o^n and pass Q_a + Q_deep to the ice as Q_o->i. If the SST carried into the step is below the freezing point T_f = 271.25 K, the SST is set to T_f and C_o (T_o* - T_f) / dt_mix is added to Q_o->i, whose negative value grows ice; otherwise the trial value is kept, and without restoring ice-covered points are held at T_f in the same way. The SST is then replaced by T_clim when there is no prognostic ocean, kept from the budget by default, or relaxed toward T_clim by the optional Newtonian restoring flux Q_R = rho_o c_p,o H (T_clim - T_o) / tau, applied according to the actual and climatological ice and followed by the T_f floor. T_o, H and Q_o->i return to the sea ice, whose ledger consumes Q_o->i in its next step and passes down the next Q_a.
